title: [Synthetic normal] Library workshop — four speakers
reference_status: Assistant-authored synthetic listening trial; not native-speaker validated

people.name: Maya
people.style: Adult woman, clear natural British English, calm meeting chair. Conversational, not a narrator.

people.name: Daniel
people.style: Adult man, natural British English, thoughtful engineer. Conversational, not a narrator.

people.name: Sofia
people.style: Adult woman, natural English with a light Spanish accent, friendly and precise. Conversational.

people.name: Omar
people.style: Adult man, natural English with an Egyptian accent, warm low register. Conversational.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Morning, everyone. Maya here. Let's settle the library workshop for Saturday. We have ten minutes, and I'd like to leave with a room, a budget, and clear owners.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Hi, it's Daniel. I checked the laptop room yesterday. The computers work, but only twelve machines have the spreadsheet software installed.

turns.speaker: sofia
turns.text: Sofia here. We have eighteen people registered. Six said they can bring their own laptop, so twelve library computers should be enough.

turns.speaker: omar
turns.text: And Omar here. Before we count on that, did those six people actually confirm? The registration form only asked whether they might bring one.

turns.speaker: sofia
turns.text: Good catch. Five confirmed by email. I am still waiting for the sixth person. I can call them after this meeting.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Then we have one potential shortage, not six. Daniel, is there a spare machine we could borrow for the afternoon?

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Yes. Reception has a spare, but I need permission before moving it. I can ask today and test the software tomorrow.

turns.speaker: omar
turns.text: The original booking says Saturday at two. The children's reading group finishes at two, though, and they need time to clear the room.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Let's start at half past two instead. Is the room free until four thirty? I don't want us packing up halfway through the exercise.

turns.speaker: omar
turns.text: It is. I checked with the librarian this morning. The two thirty to four thirty slot is available; she is holding it until tomorrow.

turns.speaker: sofia
turns.text: That works for the attendees. I'll send a corrected invitation, but I won't send it until Omar confirms the booking.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Could we use the upstairs meeting room and start at two as originally planned? It would avoid another email.

turns.speaker: omar
turns.text: The lift is being serviced on Saturday. One attendee uses a wheelchair, so the upstairs room isn't an accessible option.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Then we stay on the ground floor. Accessibility comes first. The confirmed decision is Saturday, two thirty to four thirty, in the laptop room.

turns.speaker: sofia
turns.text: Understood. The draft catering estimate is a hundred and eighty pounds. That includes sandwiches. Do we really need a meal for a two-hour workshop?

turns.speaker: omar
turns.text: Probably not. Tea, coffee, fruit, and biscuits would be ninety pounds. Water is already available, and we can label the allergens.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Let's cap refreshments at ninety pounds. No sandwiches. Omar, please check the dietary requests before placing the order.

turns.speaker: omar
turns.text: I can do that by Thursday at noon. If the special dietary options push it over ninety, I'll come back to you before ordering.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: For the exercise, I was planning to use the real volunteer contact list. It's a good example of messy data.

turns.speaker: sofia
turns.text: Let's not put personal details on shared computers. Could you make a fictional list with the same kinds of errors instead?

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Yes, absolutely. I'll replace it with fictional names and addresses. I'll test the exercise and the spare laptop by Friday at three.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Thank you. Sofia, once Omar confirms the room, please send the invitation with the new time and the ground-floor entrance instructions.

turns.speaker: sofia
turns.text: I'll send it by Thursday at four. I'll also call the attendee about bringing their laptop today. Is printed material covered by the refreshments budget?

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: No, printing is a separate existing allowance. Please don't take it out of the ninety pounds. We'll use large-print copies where requested.

turns.speaker: omar
turns.text: I will confirm the room this afternoon and message Sofia straight away. One thing is still open: whether we can offer childcare. The volunteer hasn't replied.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Keep childcare marked as unconfirmed. Don't include it as a promise in the invitation. We can send an update if someone agrees to cover it.

turns.speaker: daniel
turns.text: Just checking my list: permission for the spare laptop, a fictional dataset, and the full exercise tested by Friday at three. That's all mine.

turns.speaker: sofia
turns.text: And I have the laptop confirmation call today and the corrected invitation by Thursday at four, after the room is confirmed.

turns.speaker: omar
turns.text: I have the room confirmation today and dietary checks by Thursday at noon. Refreshments must stay within ninety pounds.

turns.speaker: maya
turns.text: Great. Saturday two thirty, ground floor, ninety pounds for refreshments. Childcare is still undecided. Thanks, everyone; we'll check any remaining issues on Friday.

facts.text: Saturday 14:30–16:30, accessible ground-floor laptop room; upstairs rejected.
Refreshments capped at GBP 90; printing separate; no sandwiches.
Daniel: spare laptop permission and fictional dataset/exercise tested by Friday 15:00.
Sofia: laptop confirmation today, invitation Thursday 16:00 after booking.
Omar: room confirmation today, dietary checks Thursday noon.
Childcare is unconfirmed; invitation must not promise it.
